question: Which kind of model can you use to respond to visual input?
explanation: What decides it is the input a model accepts, not its vendor. A multimodal model takes image-based (and in some cases audio-based) input as well as text, so it can respond to a picture. Microsoft Foundry offers such models from several providers: Microsoft Phi-4-multimodal-instruct sits next to OpenAI gpt-4.1 and gpt-4.1-mini. That is why "only OpenAI GPT models" is the trap here.

options.why: Unit 4.1.2 also lists Microsoft Phi-4-multimodal-instruct as a vision-capable model, so GPT models are not the only option.
Embedding models return vectors, not a response; unit 4.1.2 names multimodal generative models as the ones that handle image prompts.
Unit 4.1.2: to handle prompts that include images, you deploy a multimodal model, which supports image-based input as well as text.

question: How can you submit a prompt that asks a model to analyze an image?
answer: In one prompt with a **multi-part user message** that holds both a text item and an image item.
explanation: Both wrong options split the question and the image apart, into two prompts or into system and user message. The course keeps them together: the user message's content is a list with a text item (the question) and an image item, sent in one prompt. The system or developer message keeps only the text instructions. The item types are `input_text` / `input_image` in the Responses API and `text` / `image_url` in the ChatCompletions API.

options.text: Submit one prompt with an image-based message followed by another prompt with a text-based message.
options.why: Unit 4.1.3: the text and the image go into the same user message of one prompt, not into two separate prompts.

options.text: Submit a prompt that contains a multi-part user message, containing both text content and image content.
options.why: Unit 4.1.3: prompts for a vision-based chat include multi-part user messages with a text content item and an image content item.

options.text: Submit the image as the system message and the instruction or question as the user message.
options.why: Unit 4.1.3's code keeps the system (or developer) message for text instructions and puts the image in the user message.

question: How can you include an image in a message?
answer: **As a URL or as binary data** (Base64-encoded in a data URL).
explanation: Neither form is exclusive. A web-based image goes in as its URL. A local file is read in binary mode, Base64-encoded and sent as a data URL of the form `data:image/jpeg;base64,{image_data}`, with `jpeg` replaced by `png` or another format as needed. So "binary data" here means the encoded bytes carried inside a URL. The Responses API (`input_image`) and the ChatCompletions API (`image_url`) both accept either form.

options.text: As a URL or as binary data
options.why: Unit 4.1.3: specify a URL for a web-based image, or load a local image, encode its data in Base64 and submit it as a data URL.
Unit 4.1.3 also shows sending a local image's binary data, Base64-encoded in a data URL.
Unit 4.1.3 also allows a plain URL to a web-based image file.
